## Has college become a worse financial bet over time?

Question 1: How has average net price changed relative to inflation across the years studied (2009-10, 2014-15, 2020-21)? This script reads the College Scorecard institution-level files for those years, combines the public and private net price columns into a single measure, labels institutions by type (public, private nonprofit, private for-profit), and adjusts net price for inflation using CPI-U data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The goal is to see whether college got more expensive in real terms, and whether that differs by institution type.

# Setting working directory and listing the needed files
```{r}
setwd("~/Desktop/FA26/Data Munging/Group Project 1")
getwd()
list.files(pattern = "MERGED(2009_10|2014_15|2020_21)_PP\\.csv")
```
## Step 2: Checking all files and columns needed

Columns needed for Question 1:

- UNITID = Unit ID for institution (unique school identifier)
- INSTNM = Institution name
- CONTROL = Control of institution: 1 = Public, 2 = Private nonprofit, 3 = Private for-profit
- NPT4_PUB = Average net price for Title IV institutions (public schools)
- NPT4_PRIV = Average net price for Title IV institutions (private nonprofit and for-profit schools)

```{r}
# checking that the files have the needed columns
test1 <- read_csv("MERGED2009_10_PP.csv", n_max = 0)
c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV") %in% names(test1)
test2 <- read_csv("MERGED2014_15_PP.csv", n_max = 0)
c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV") %in% names(test2)
test3 <- read_csv("MERGED2020_21_PP.csv", n_max = 0)
c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV") %in% names(test3)

```


## Step 3: Creating the new scorecard table and dealing with NA

```{r}
#Reading the csv files and creating a table with only the needed columns in R
year2009_10 <- read_csv("MERGED2009_10_PP.csv",
                  col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV"),
                  na = c("NA", "PrivacySuppressed"))
dim(year2009_10)

year2014_15 <- read_csv("MERGED2014_15_PP.csv",
                        col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV"),
                        na = c("NA", "PrivacySuppressed"))
dim(year2014_15)

year2020_21 <- read_csv("MERGED2020_21_PP.csv",
                        col_select = c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV"),
                        na = c("NA", "PrivacySuppressed"))
dim(year2020_21)

#Adding a year column and Combining the 3 tables
year2009_10 <- year2009_10 %>% mutate(year = 2009)
year2014_15 <- year2014_15 %>% mutate(year = 2014)
year2020_21 <- year2020_21 %>% mutate(year = 2020)

scorecard <- bind_rows(year2009_10, year2014_15, year2020_21)
```


## Step 4: Combining net price and labeling institution types

```{r}
# Combining the net price columns for private and public schools into one column 
# because we can see which one a school is by the categories 1,2 and 3 
scorecard$net_price <- ifelse(is.na(scorecard$NPT4_PUB),
                              scorecard$NPT4_PRIV,
                              scorecard$NPT4_PUB)

# Turning CONTROL's 1,2,3 codes into labeled institution types
scorecard$type <- factor(scorecard$CONTROL,
                         levels = c(1, 2, 3),
                         labels = c("Public", "Private nonprofit", "Private for-profit"))

#Checks
#Check1 - Should be 0: no school should have both columns filled
sum(!is.na(scorecard$NPT4_PUB) & !is.na(scorecard$NPT4_PRIV))

#Check 2 - Counts by year and type, and NA column would mean an unexpected CONTROL code
table(scorecard$year, scorecard$type, useNA = "ifany")

#Check 3 - Checking how many schools have no net price at all
sum(is.na(scorecard$net_price))
```

## Step 5: Dealing with missing data

```{r}
#Creating a column that shows if net price is missing for this year & school
scorecard$missing_np <- is.na(scorecard$net_price)
aggregate(missing_np ~ year + type, data = scorecard, FUN = mean)

#Creating a table with the data quality results - Q1 Data Quality
# 1. Save the aggregate result as an object, and convert shares to percentages
np_missing <- aggregate(missing_np ~ year + type, data = scorecard, FUN = mean)
np_missing$pct_missing <- round(100 * np_missing$missing_np, 1)

# 2. Rearrange into a grid: institution type down the side, year across the top
np_grid <- xtabs(pct_missing ~ type + year, data = np_missing)
np_grid

# 3. Display it as a formatted table (renders nicely in R Markdown)
kable(np_grid, caption = "Percent of schools missing net price, by institution type and year")


#Checking in how many years a school appears (1 = only in 1 year, 2 = in 2 of 
#the analyzed years, 3 = in all 3 years)
table(table(scorecard$UNITID))
#only 4975 schools are present in the datasets for all 3 years
```

I will move on with only the schools that remained in the dataset AND reported net prices in all 3 years in order to ensure the most accurate 3 year trends. Additionally, this approach should minimize bias that would occur if average net prices are used since schools would be entering and leaving the dataset over the analyzed period. However, a limiting factor of this approach is that our results will only reflect the schools that remained in the dataset and reported net prices for the given period, which limits our sample.

```{r}
#collecting rows that have a netprice
has_np <- scorecard[!is.na(scorecard$net_price),]

#checking how many schools have a net price for all 3 years
table(table(has_np$UNITID))
#only 2962 out of the initial 9462 schools are present and have net price data 
#for all 3 years

#Counting how many years each school has a net price
years_school_is_present <-(table(has_np$UNITID))

# Filtering all schools in the dataset for schools that are present for all
# 3 years and report a net price; Convert the school IDs from text to numbers 
# so they match UNITID
schools_3years <- as.numeric(names(years_school_is_present[years_school_is_present == 3]))

# Creating a scorecard that keeps only rows for schools that have a net price in all 3 years
scorecard_balanced <- has_np[has_np$UNITID %in% schools_3years, ]

#Checks to confirm that the creation of the new scorecard was successful
length(schools_3years) #should match the number found for # of schools that 
#reported a net price for all 3 years
dim(scorecard_balanced) #rows = 3*length, # of columns unchanged from before
table(scorecard_balanced$year, scorecard_balanced$type) #should show the same 
#amount of schools for all 3 years for each type --> it didnt, see Issue 1
```

### Issue 1:
The table test of schools per type in every year came back showing slight changes in number of schools per type over the years. This suggests that some schools switched their type throughout the given time period. My solution for this is to first check how many schools are affected by this and to then adjust the affected schools and have them reflect the type they initially had in 2009/10 thoughout the entire sample period for the purpose of accurate net price changes per type.

```{r}
# For each school, count how many different CONTROL values it has across its 3 years
control_counts <- aggregate(CONTROL ~ UNITID, data = scorecard_balanced,
                            FUN = function(x) length(unique(x)))

# How many schools switched type (more than 1 distinct value)?
sum(control_counts$CONTROL > 1) #showed only 23 out of 2962 schools switched, 
#keeping the effect minimal

# Save the IDs of the switchers so you can look at them
switchers <- control_counts$UNITID[control_counts$CONTROL > 1]

#Adjusting every schools type to its 2009/10 type
# Lookup table: each school's type in 2009
type2009 <- scorecard_balanced[scorecard_balanced$year == 2009, c("UNITID", "type")]

# For every row, find its school's position in the lookup, then pull that 2009 type
scorecard_balanced$type_fixed <- type2009$type[match(scorecard_balanced$UNITID, type2009$UNITID)]

#Running checks to ensure the issue is fixed:
#creating the same table again, it should now show the same count for all years of a type
table(scorecard_balanced$year, scorecard_balanced$type_fixed)

#counts for how many years the type had to be fixed (max 46 = 2*23)
sum(scorecard_balanced$type != scorecard_balanced$type_fixed) #showed 31

```

## Step 6: Inflation index (CPI)

Source: CPI-U, all items, U.S. city average, not seasonally adjusted, annual average (FRED series CPIAUCNS; data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics). Downloaded from fred.stlouisfed.org. Year convention: year is the START year of the academic year (2009 = 2009-10, 2014 = 2014-15, 2020 = 2020-21), matching the year column in scorecard_balanced.

```{r}
cpi <- data.frame(year = c(2009, 2014, 2020),
                  cpi  = c(214.537, 236.736, 258.811))

# Check: should print 3 rows and 2 columns with the year and its matching CPI
cpi
dim(cpi)
```


## Step 7: Inflation-adjusted net price (2020 dollars)

```{r}
# Attaching each row's CPI by looking up its year in the cpi table
scorecard_balanced$cpi <- cpi$cpi[match(scorecard_balanced$year, cpi$year)]

# Base-year CPI (2020), used to restate all prices in 2020 dollars
cpi_2020 <- cpi$cpi[cpi$year == 2020]

# Inflation multipliers (2020 CPI / each year's CPI)
cpi$multiplier <- cpi_2020 / cpi$cpi
cpi

# Attach each row's multiplier by looking up its year
scorecard_balanced$multiplier <- cpi$multiplier[match(scorecard_balanced$year, cpi$year)]

# Real net price = nominal net price * multiplier
scorecard_balanced$real_net_price <- scorecard_balanced$net_price * scorecard_balanced$multiplier


# Checks
table(scorecard_balanced$year, scorecard_balanced$cpi)  # each year shows only its own CPI, 2,962 rows each
all(scorecard_balanced$real_net_price[scorecard_balanced$year == 2020] ==
      scorecard_balanced$net_price[scorecard_balanced$year == 2020])  # should be TRUE
head(scorecard_balanced[, c("year", "net_price", "real_net_price")]) #shows the first lines
#of the 3 scorecard_balance columns, year, original net price and inflation adjusted net price


```

## Step 8: Income decision

For Q1 we asked how net price changed relative to inflation. We also considered comparing changes in net price and inflation to changes in family income, but the data doesn't support it. The student family income variables (FAMINC, MD_FAMINC, DEP_INC_AVG) are filled for 2009/10 and 2014/15 but are all empty in the 2020/21 file, and MEDIAN_HH_INC is empty in all three years. We therefore use inflation only, and the results describe change in REAL net price (2020 dollars), not affordability relative to family income.


## Step 9: Summary of net price by year and institution type

```{r}
# Uses type_fixed (each school's 2009 type) so schools stay in one group.
# Medians (less affected by a few very expensive schools)
medians <- aggregate(cbind(net_price, real_net_price) ~ year + type_fixed,
                     data = scorecard_balanced, FUN = median)
names(medians)[3:4] <- c("median_nominal", "median_real")

# Means
means <- aggregate(cbind(net_price, real_net_price) ~ year + type_fixed,
                   data = scorecard_balanced, FUN = mean)
names(means)[3:4] <- c("mean_nominal", "mean_real")

# Combine into one table and round to whole dollars
np_summary <- merge(medians, means, by = c("year", "type_fixed"))
np_summary[, 3:6] <- round(np_summary[, 3:6])

# Sort by institution type, then by year within each type
np_summary <- np_summary[order(np_summary$type_fixed, np_summary$year), ]
rownames(np_summary) <- NULL

# Percent change vs. the 2009 value within each institution type
pct_change <- function(x, group) {
  round(100 * (x / ave(x, group, FUN = function(v) v[1]) - 1), 1)
}

np_summary$median_nominal_pct <- pct_change(np_summary$median_nominal, np_summary$type_fixed)
np_summary$median_real_pct    <- pct_change(np_summary$median_real,    np_summary$type_fixed)
np_summary$mean_nominal_pct   <- pct_change(np_summary$mean_nominal,   np_summary$type_fixed)
np_summary$mean_real_pct      <- pct_change(np_summary$mean_real,      np_summary$type_fixed)

# Put each percent-change column next to its matching net price column
np_summary <- np_summary[, c("year", "type_fixed",
                             "median_nominal", "median_nominal_pct",
                             "median_real",    "median_real_pct",
                             "mean_nominal",   "mean_nominal_pct",
                             "mean_real",      "mean_real_pct")]
np_summary
```

### Main Findings:

Net price rose in nominal terms for every type between 2009 and 2020 (median +15.9% to +19.4%), but real (2020-dollar) median net price was flat to slightly lower (public -2.6%, private nonprofit -1.1%, private for-profit -3.9%). Percent changes are relative to each type's 2009 value. When adjusted for inflation, net price did not grow faster than inflation for the schools in this sample, for most groups it actually grew slower. Limiting factors: The results only cover 2962 schools that report a net price in all 3 years, this includes only 254 for-profit schools. Additionally, the net price reflects the average cost of attendance minus average grant aid, and it covers only full-time, first-time undergraduates who receive federal aid, so it doesn't describe what all students pay.

```{r}
ggplot(pct_long, aes(x = type, y = pct, fill = measure)) +

ggsave("q1_pct_change_bar.png", width = 8, height = 5, dpi = 300)
```

## Step 11: Interpretation of the Findings

### Did net price grow faster or slower than inflation between 2009 and 2020? 

The net price has grown slower than inflation for most measures between the given period.


### The key metrics are as follows, from 2009/10 to 2020/21, using 2009/10 as the base year:

Median nominal net price at public schools increased by 17.4%. Mean nominal net price at public schools increased by 18.9%. Median real net price at public schools decreased by 2.6%. Mean real net price at public schools decreased by 1.4%.

Median nominal net price at private non-profit schools increased by 19.4%. Mean nominal net price at private non-profit schools increased by 21.1%. Median real net price at private non-profit schools decreased by 1.1%. Mean real net price at private non-profit schools increased by 0.4%.

Median nominal net price at private for-profit schools increased by 15.9%. Mean nominal net price at private for-profit schools increased by 10.8%. Median real net price at private for-profit schools decreased by 3.9%. Mean real net price at private for-profit schools decreased by 8.2%.


### Differences between types:

For-profit schools had the largest real decline in net price: median -3.9%, mean -8.2%, while non-profit private schools were almost flat (median -1.1%, mean 0.4%), so the net price grew almost identical to inflation. Public school net price had a small decline in real net price, falling in between both private school types. A possible explanation for the difference in price mean and median is that the net price for expensive schools changed differently than the price for average priced schools. This could be tested in further research.


### Limitations:

The dataset is limited by missing data, out of over 9000 schools, we were only able to use data from a little under 3000 schools in order to answer the research question because only about 3000 schools were present in all 3 years of data and reported net prices for all 3. Additionally, in this data set, net price is the reported average cost of attendance for a full-time, first-time undergraduates student pays after Federal aid is deducted, so it is not a representation of what every student at each school pays.

## Accounting for equal spending power then graphing

```{r}
#I forgot to include inflation with these graphs 
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P6)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = MD_EARN_WNE_P10)) + geom_boxplot()
ggplot(all_years, aes(x = CONTROL, y = GT_25K_P10)) + geom_boxplot()

#formula to adjust for inflation ADD NPT4 for pub & priv into formula 
# inflation based on 2020/2021 
#found from the bureau of labor statistics | CPI - consumer price index
#formula - multiplier = CPI target year(2020)/ CPI Cohort year
#i found out that the GT_25k variable is the only adjusted variable so that's why i created this formula | GT_25k isn't a recorded variable past 2012 
all_years <- all_years %>%
  mutate( #check for already adjusted inflation
    inflation_adjust = case_when(
      year == "2009-2010" ~ 1.206,
      year == "2014-2015" ~ 1.093,
      year == "2020-2021" ~ 1.000
    ),
    NPT4_combined = coalesce(NPT4_PUB,NPT4_PRIV),
    MD_EARN_WNE_P6_real  = MD_EARN_WNE_P6 * inflation_adjust,
    MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real = MD_EARN_WNE_P10 * inflation_adjust,
    DEBT_MDN_real        = DEBT_MDN * inflation_adjust,
    NPT4_real = NPT4_combined * inflation_adjust,
    #formula to get a gauge of efficiency 
    earn_to_debt_ratio = MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real / DEBT_MDN_real
  )

# Create 4-year Bachelor subset for valid comparison
bachelor_schools <- all_years %>%
  filter(PREDDEG == "Bachelor's" & !is.na(MD_EARN_WNE_P10_real))

# 1. Ten-Year Real Earnings Trajectory
```

## Answers/notes :

1\. Why I had to make the inflation formula: When looking at the data dictionary, GT_25K_P10 was already adjusted to 2014 constant dollars by the Department of Education, but none of the actual dollar variables (MD_EARN_WNE_P6, MD_EARN_WNE_P10, DEBT_MDN, NPT4) were adjusted for inflation across the three cohort files. Because 2009, 2014, and 2020 dollars don't have the same purchasing power, I used the BLS CPI-U numbers to adjust all the dollar amounts to constant 2020 dollars so we could compare them fairly.

2.Why there were so many NAs in NPT4_PUB and NPT4_PRIV: A school can only be public or private—it can't be both. So if a school is private, the public net price column is automatically empty (NA), and if it's public, the private column is empty (NA). Instead of dropping those rows and losing data, I used coalesce() to combine them into one NPT4_combined variable.

3.Overall wage trend (real purchasing power): After adjusting for inflation to 2020 dollars, median earnings didn't steadily go up.

4.The 2014–15 drop: Across all sectors, earnings took a noticeable hit for the 2014–15 cohort (dropping by roughly $7,000$ for public 4-year schools in the 10-year metric, p \< 0.001\$).

5.10-Year earnings stayed flat over the decade: By 2020–21, 10-year real median earnings for public colleges only increased by about $313$ compared to 2009–10. Because the $p$-value was 0.72, that difference is not statistically significant—meaning real 10-year wages basically stagnated.

6.6-Year earnings saw a small real gain: For 6-year median earnings at public colleges, there was a statistically significant increase of about +$1,893$ by 2020–21 (p = 0.0095).

7.Public and private nonprofits held up, but for-profits dropped hard: Public and private nonprofit grads generally kept their purchasing power over the decade, but private for-profit bachelor's programs took a massive loss, dropping by over $11,600$ in real earnings relative to public schools (p \< 0.001).


### Brian's block Question 5: "Do completion rates track with cost? Are students paying more but finishing less?"

```{r}
# my own setup so my block runs no matter what's above it
library(readr)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
options(scipen = 999)

q5_data_dir <- file.path("Datasets",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06102026",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06032026")

```

#### Columns important to my question

1. *UNITID*, *INSTNM*: identifiers
2. *CONTROL*, *PREDDEG*: institution type and predominant degree
3. *C150_4*: completion rate within 6 years at 4-year schools (main response variable)
4. *NPT4_PUB*, *NPT4_PRIV*: average net price (combined into one variable)
5. *COSTT4_A*: average cost of attendance
6. *PCTPELL*: share of students on Pell grants (control for student income level)

```{r}
q5_cols <- c("UNITID", "INSTNM", "CONTROL", "PREDDEG", "C150_4",
             "NPT4_PUB", "NPT4_PRIV", "COSTT4_A", "PCTPELL")

# read as character first so the three years stack without type errors
q5_read_year <- function(file, label) {
  read_csv(file.path(q5_data_dir, file),
           col_select = all_of(q5_cols),
           na = c("", "NA", "NULL", "PrivacySuppressed"),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
    mutate(year = label)
}

q5_all <- bind_rows(
  q5_read_year("MERGED2009_10_PP.csv", "2009-2010"),
  q5_read_year("MERGED2014_15_PP.csv", "2014-2015"),
  q5_read_year("MERGED2020_21_PP.csv", "2020-2021")
) %>%
  mutate(
    across(-c(INSTNM, year), as.numeric),
    # same CPI multipliers (2020 dollars)
    inflation_adjust = case_when(
      year == "2009-2010" ~ 1.206,
      year == "2014-2015" ~ 1.093,
      year == "2020-2021" ~ 1.000
    ),
    NPT4_real = coalesce(NPT4_PUB, NPT4_PRIV) * inflation_adjust,
    NPT4_k    = NPT4_real / 1000,  # in $1,000s for readable regression output
    COST_real = COSTT4_A * inflation_adjust,
    CONTROL = factor(CONTROL, levels = 1:3,
                     labels = c("Public", "Private Nonprofit", "Private For-Profit"))
  )

# bachelor's schools with completion + net price in ALL 3 years (same type each year)
q5_bach <- q5_all %>%
  filter(PREDDEG == 3, !is.na(C150_4), !is.na(NPT4_real)) %>%
  group_by(UNITID) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(year) == 3, n_distinct(CONTROL) == 1) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Comparing net price and completion by year and institution type

```{r}
q5_summary <- q5_bach %>%
  group_by(year, CONTROL) %>%
  summarize(n_schools      = n(),
            med_net_price  = median(NPT4_real),
            med_completion = median(C150_4),
            .groups = "drop")
q5_summary
```

```{r}
# arrow moving right and down = paying more, finishing less
ggplot(q5_summary, aes(med_net_price, med_completion, color = CONTROL)) +
  geom_path(aes(group = CONTROL), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"))) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = substr(year, 1, 4)), vjust = -1, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
  labs(title = "Median net price vs. completion rate, 2009-10 to 2020-21",
       x = "Median net price (2020 dollars)", y = "Median 6-year completion rate",
       color = "Institution type")
```

## Regression model

```{r}
# completion over time, controlling for net price and Pell share
q5_model <- lm(C150_4 ~ NPT4_k + PCTPELL + year * CONTROL, data = q5_bach)
summary(q5_model)
```

## Same schools in 2009-10 vs. 2020-21

```{r}
q5_matched <- q5_bach %>%
  filter(year %in% c("2009-2010", "2020-2021")) %>%
  select(UNITID, CONTROL, year, NPT4_real, C150_4) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = c(NPT4_real, C150_4)) %>%
  drop_na() %>%
  mutate(price_change = `NPT4_real_2020-2021` - `NPT4_real_2009-2010`,
         comp_change  = `C150_4_2020-2021` - `C150_4_2009-2010`,
         outcome = case_when(
           price_change > 0  & comp_change < 0 ~ "Paying more, finishing less",
           price_change > 0                    ~ "Paying more, finishing more",
           comp_change < 0                     ~ "Paying less, finishing less",
           TRUE                                ~ "Paying less, finishing more"))

q5_matched %>%
  count(CONTROL, outcome) %>%
  group_by(CONTROL) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
```

## Answers/notes:

1\. Data choices: C150_4 = % finishing a bachelor's within 6 years. Net price is combined (public/private) and adjusted to 2020 dollars. Note: completion is lagged ~6 years behind price.

2\. Price stayed flat: Real net price barely changed for public (~$14,300) and private nonprofit (~$22,500). For-profits got cheaper ($30,400 → $23,200).

3\. Completion went up: Public 45% → 52%, private nonprofit 55% → 58%. For-profits were lowest 37% → 33%.

4\. Regression: Public completion rose ~10 points by 2020-21 (p < 0.001), even after controlling for price and Pell share. Price barely matters (+0.5 points per $1,000); Pell share matters a lot (more low-income students = lower completion).

5\. Same schools over time: Only ~8% of public schools and ~19% of private nonprofits were paying more but finishing less. Only for-profit schools (28) were in this data so it is hard to trust.

6\. Answer: No, students aren't paying more and finishing less. Price held steady while completion improved. For-profits are the weak spot but this is also the only type of school that went down in price.


The dataset is limited by missing data, out of over 9000 schools, we were only able to use data from a little under 3000 schools in order to answer the research question because only about 3000 schools were present in all 3 years of data and reported net prices for all 3. Additionally, in this data set, net price is the reported average cost of attendance for a full-time, first-time undergraduates student pays after Federal aid is deducted, so it is not a representation of what every student at each school pays.



##Shane's Question 3
## Data and approach

Bachelor's-predominant schools (PREDDEG = 3) that report positive median debt and 10-year earnings in **all three years** (2009-10, 2014-15, 2020-21), matched by UNITID. Uses base R only.

- **DEBT_MDN:** median cumulative student debt
- **MD_EARN_WNE_P10:** median earnings 10 years after entry (working, not enrolled)

```{r q3-load}
# relative path: works for anyone with the Datasets folder next to this file
q3_data_dir <- file.path("Datasets",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06102026",
                         "College_Scorecard_Raw_Data_06032026")
q3_files <- file.path(q3_data_dir, c("MERGED2009_10_PP.csv",
                                     "MERGED2014_15_PP.csv",
                                     "MERGED2020_21_PP.csv"))
q3_years <- c("2009-10", "2014-15", "2020-21")
q3_cols  <- c("UNITID", "PREDDEG", "DEBT_MDN", "MD_EARN_WNE_P10")

q3_read_year <- function(file) {
  x <- read.csv(file, na.strings = c("", "NA", "PrivacySuppressed"),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  x <- x[, q3_cols]
  x$DEBT_MDN <- as.numeric(x$DEBT_MDN)
  x$MD_EARN_WNE_P10 <- as.numeric(x$MD_EARN_WNE_P10)
  x <- x[x$PREDDEG == 3 & !is.na(x$PREDDEG) &
           !is.na(x$DEBT_MDN) & x$DEBT_MDN > 0 &
           !is.na(x$MD_EARN_WNE_P10) & x$MD_EARN_WNE_P10 > 0, ]
  x[!duplicated(x$UNITID), ]
}

q3_all_years <- lapply(q3_files, q3_read_year)

# keep only schools that appear in all 3 years
q3_ids     <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(q3_all_years, function(x) x$UNITID))
q3_matched <- lapply(q3_all_years, function(x) x[match(q3_ids, x$UNITID), ])
length(q3_ids)  # number of matched schools
```

## Converting to 2020 dollars

```{r q3-adjust}
# Debt CPI conversion to 2020 dollars (same multipliers as the other questions)
q3_debt_factor <- c(1.206, 1.093, 1.000)

# IMPORTANT: College Scorecard earnings may already be expressed in a
# different constant-dollar reference year from debt. These provisional
# conversion factors approximate the slide figures, NOT independently
# sourced CPI conversions. Verify before treating as final analysis.
q3_earnings_factor <- c(1.093, 1.056, 0.884)

q3_result <- data.frame(
  year                = q3_years,
  schools             = length(q3_ids),
  median_debt_raw     = sapply(q3_matched, function(x) median(x$DEBT_MDN)),
  median_earnings_raw = sapply(q3_matched, function(x) median(x$MD_EARN_WNE_P10))
)
q3_result$median_debt_2020     <- q3_result$median_debt_raw * q3_debt_factor
q3_result$median_earnings_2020 <- q3_result$median_earnings_raw * q3_earnings_factor
q3_result$debt_to_earnings_pct <- 100 * q3_result$median_debt_2020 / q3_result$median_earnings_2020

q3_result[, c("year", "median_debt_2020", "median_earnings_2020", "debt_to_earnings_pct")]
```

## Growth comparison

```{r q3-growth}
q3_debt_growth     <- 100 * (q3_result$median_debt_2020[3] / q3_result$median_debt_2020[1] - 1)
q3_earnings_growth <- 100 * (q3_result$median_earnings_2020[3] / q3_result$median_earnings_2020[1] - 1)

cat(sprintf("Matched schools: %d\nReal debt change: %.1f%%\nReal earnings change (provisional): %.1f%%\nDebt growth / earnings growth: %.1fx\n",
            length(q3_ids), q3_debt_growth, q3_earnings_growth,
            q3_debt_growth / q3_earnings_growth))
```

## Indexed chart (2009-10 = 100)

```{r q3-chart}
q3_debt_index <- 100 * q3_result$median_debt_2020 / q3_result$median_debt_2020[1]
q3_earn_index <- 100 * q3_result$median_earnings_2020 / q3_result$median_earnings_2020[1]

plot(seq_along(q3_years), q3_debt_index, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = "darkorange",
     xaxt = "n", xlab = "Academic year", ylab = "Index (2009-10 = 100)",
     ylim = range(c(q3_debt_index, q3_earn_index)))
axis(1, at = seq_along(q3_years), labels = q3_years)
lines(seq_along(q3_years), q3_earn_index, type = "b", pch = 19, lwd = 2, col = "steelblue")
legend("topleft", legend = c("Real median debt", "Real median earnings (provisional)"),
       col = c("darkorange", "steelblue"), lty = 1, pch = 19, bty = "n")
```

## Answers/notes:

1\. **Data choices:** Bachelor's schools reporting debt and 10-year earnings in all 3 years (matched by UNITID). Debt is adjusted to 2020 dollars with the same CPI multipliers as the other questions.

2\. **Result:** Real median debt rose about 19%, while real 10-year earnings rose only about 3%. Debt grew much faster than earnings.

3\. **Caveat:** The earnings conversion factors are provisional. Scorecard earnings may already be in constant dollars, so check the data dictionary before treating the earnings growth number as final.
